sets.title: Set 1: Equations of Motion (Constant Acceleration)
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Equations of Motion (Constant Acceleration)

questions.prompt: What is the third kinematic equation connecting velocities $u$, $v$, acceleration $a$, and displacement $s$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Motion in a Straight Line
questions.explanation: Eliminating $t$ between $v = u + at$ and $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ yields the fundamental relation: $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.

questions.prompt: Which equation gives the displacement $s_n$ traversed in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second?
questions.subPrompt: Displacement in n-th second
questions.explanation: Subtracting displacement at $(n-1)$ seconds from displacement at $n$ seconds gives: $s_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$.

questions.prompt: What is the displacement formula for a body moving with initial velocity $u$ and uniform acceleration $a$?
questions.subPrompt: Second Kinematic Equation
questions.explanation: Integrating $v = u + at$ with respect to time $t$ gives $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.

questions.prompt: For a body starting from rest ($u = 0$) under uniform acceleration, what is the ratio of distances traveled in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd seconds (Galileo's Odd Ratio)?
questions.subPrompt: Galileo's Law of Odd Numbers
questions.explanation: Using $s_n = \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$, for $n = 1, 2, 3$, the distances are proportional to odd numbers $1 : 3 : 5 : 7\dots$.

questions.prompt: What is the stopping distance $d_s$ of a vehicle of mass $m$ with speed $v$ and braking force $F$?
questions.subPrompt: Work-Energy Stopping Formula
questions.explanation: Equating initial kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ to braking work $F \cdot d_s$ gives $d_s = \frac{mv^2}{2F} = \frac{v^2}{2a}$.

questions.prompt: If a body travels first half distance with speed $v_1$ and remaining half with speed $v_2$, what is its average speed?
questions.subPrompt: Harmonic Mean of Speeds
questions.explanation: Total distance $D$, total time $T = \frac{D/2}{v_1} + \frac{D/2}{v_2} = \frac{D(v_1+v_2)}{2v_1 v_2}$. Thus $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}$.

questions.prompt: What does the slope of a displacement-time ($x$-$t$) graph represent?
questions.subPrompt: Calculus Interpretation of Slope
questions.explanation: By calculus definition, the derivative (slope) of position with respect to time is instantaneous velocity $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What does the area enclosed under an acceleration-time ($a$-$t$) graph represent?
questions.subPrompt: Definite Integral Interpretation
questions.explanation: Since $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$, the area under $a$-$t$ is $\int a\,dt = v_2 - v_1 = \Delta v$ (change in velocity).

questions.prompt: For an object thrown vertically upward with initial speed $u$, what is the maximum height $H_{\max}$ reached?
questions.subPrompt: Motion Under Gravity
questions.explanation: At maximum height, $v = 0$. Using $v^2 = u^2 - 2gH_{\max} \implies 0 = u^2 - 2gH_{\max} \implies H_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{2g}$.

questions.prompt: What is the total time of flight $T$ for a particle projected vertically upwards with speed $u$?
questions.subPrompt: Time of Ascent and Descent
questions.explanation: Time of ascent $t_a = \frac{u}{g}$ and time of descent $t_d = \frac{u}{g}$. Total time of flight $T = t_a + t_d = \frac{2u}{g}$.

sets.title: Set 2: Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall

questions.prompt: What is the optimum banking angle $\theta$ for a curved road of radius $R$ designed for speed $v$ without relying on friction?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Balancing forces: $N\sin\theta = \frac{mv^2}{R}$ and $N\cos\theta = mg$. Dividing gives $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{Rg}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between angle of friction $\theta$ and angle of repose $\alpha$ for an inclined plane?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: At the verge of sliding down, $mg\sin\alpha = \mu_s mg\cos\alpha \implies \tan\alpha = \mu_s$. Since $\tan\theta = \mu_s$, $\alpha = \theta$.

questions.prompt: What is the apparent weight $W'$ of a person of mass $m$ in an elevator accelerating downwards with acceleration $a$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: In the accelerating frame, pseudo force acts upward: $N = m(g - a)$.

questions.prompt: What is the impulse $J$ delivered by a force $\vec{F}(t)$ acting over duration $\Delta t$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Impulse equals the time integral of force and is identical to total momentum change: $\vec{J} = \Delta\vec{p}$.

questions.prompt: What is the tension $T$ in a simple Atwood machine having two masses $m_1 > m_2$ connected over a light frictionless pulley?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Acceleration $a = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$. Substituting into $T - m_2 g = m_2 a$ gives $T = \frac{2m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$.

questions.prompt: What is the acceleration $a$ of the two masses $m_1 > m_2$ in the standard Atwood machine?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Net pulling force is $(m_1 - m_2)g$. Total moving mass is $(m_1 + m_2)$. Hence $a = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$.

questions.prompt: What is the bending angle $\theta$ from the vertical for a cyclist negotiating a turn of radius $r$ at speed $v$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Torque balance about the contact point requires normal and friction torques to cancel: $\tan\theta = \frac{f}{N} = \frac{v^2}{rg}$.

questions.prompt: What is the vector expression for Newton's Second Law of Motion?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Force is defined as the time rate of change of momentum: $\vec{F} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$. For constant mass, $\vec{F} = m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = m\vec{a}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between limiting static friction $f_s^{\max}$ and normal reaction $N$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Limiting static friction is directly proportional to normal force: $f_s^{\max} = \mu_s N$.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum speed $v_{\max}$ of a car on a level circular road of radius $R$ with friction coefficient $\mu$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Motion Under Gravity & Free Fall
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is provided by friction: $\frac{mv^2}{R} \le \mu mg \implies v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu R g}$.

sets.title: Set 4: Projectile Motion: Maximum Height & Range
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Projectile Motion: Maximum Height & Range

questions.prompt: What is the horizontal range $R$ of a projectile fired with velocity $u$ at angle $\theta$ with the horizontal?
questions.subPrompt: Range of a Projectile
questions.explanation: $$R = u_x \times T = (u\cos\theta)\left(\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}\right) = \frac{u^2(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)}{g} = \frac{u^2\sin(2\theta)}{g}$$.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum vertical height $H_{\max}$ attained by a projectile fired at angle $\theta$?
questions.subPrompt: Peak Height Formula
questions.explanation: At the peak, vertical velocity $v_y = 0$. Using $v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2gH \implies H_{\max} = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$.

questions.prompt: At what projection angle $\theta$ is the horizontal range of a projectile maximum?
questions.subPrompt: Optimal Launch Angle
questions.explanation: Range $R = \frac{u^2\sin(2\theta)}{g}$. Max range occurs when $\sin(2\theta) = 1 \implies 2\theta = 90^\circ \implies \theta = 45^\circ$, giving $R_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{g}$.

questions.prompt: Two angles of projection give the same horizontal range for the same speed $u$. What is their mathematical relationship?
questions.subPrompt: Complementary Angles Theorem
questions.explanation: Since $\sin(2(90^\circ - \theta)) = \sin(180^\circ - 2\theta) = \sin(2\theta)$, complementary angles produce the exact same horizontal range.

questions.prompt: What is the standard Cartesian trajectory equation $y(x)$ of a parabolic projectile?
questions.subPrompt: Equation of Trajectory
questions.explanation: Substitute $t = \frac{x}{u\cos\theta}$ into $y = u\sin\theta\cdot t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ to get $y = x\tan\theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$.

questions.prompt: What is the alternative form of the trajectory equation in terms of horizontal range $R$?
questions.subPrompt: Range Form of Trajectory
questions.explanation: Factoring out $x\tan\theta$ from $y = x\tan\theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$ and using $R = \frac{2u^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}$ gives $y = x\tan\theta(1 - x/R)$.

questions.prompt: What is the ratio of horizontal range $R$ to maximum height $H_{\max}$ when fired at angle $\theta$?
questions.subPrompt: Range-to-Height Ratio
questions.explanation: $$\frac{R}{H} = \frac{(u^2\cdot 2\sin\theta\cos\theta)/g}{(u^2\sin^2\theta)/(2g)} = \frac{4\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} = 4\cot\theta$$.

questions.prompt: If the launch angle is $\theta = 45^\circ$, what is the relation between range $R$ and maximum height $H$?
questions.subPrompt: Special Case at 45 Degrees
questions.explanation: At $\theta = 45^\circ$, $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$. Since $R = 4H/\tan\theta$, we have $R = 4H$.

questions.prompt: What is the speed of a projectile at its highest point of trajectory?
questions.subPrompt: Peak Velocity Vector
questions.explanation: At the peak, vertical velocity $v_y = 0$, but horizontal velocity remains constant throughout flight: $v_x = u\cos\theta$.

questions.prompt: What is the centripetal acceleration $a_c$ of a body moving with speed $v$ along a circle of radius $r$?
questions.subPrompt: Circular Kinematics
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration pointing towards the center is given by $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2 r$, where $v = \omega r$.

sets.title: Set 1: Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Work Done by Constant & Variable Force

questions.prompt: What is the mathematical formulation of the Work-Energy Theorem for a particle?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: The net work done by all forces equals the change in kinetic energy: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$.

questions.prompt: What is the elastic potential energy $U_s$ stored in a spring with spring constant $k$ stretched by elongation $x$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: Integrating restoring force work: $U = \int_0^x kx\,dx = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the instantaneous power $P$ delivered by force $\vec{F}$ to a body moving with velocity $\vec{v}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: Power is rate of work done: $P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \vec{F}\cdot\frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}$.

questions.prompt: What is the final velocity $v_1$ of mass $m_1$ after a 1D head-on elastic collision with mass $m_2$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: Simultaneous conservation of linear momentum and kinetic energy gives $v_1 = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}u_1 + \frac{2m_2}{m_1 + m_2}u_2$.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum speed $v_{\text{bottom}}$ required at the lowest point of a vertical circle of radius $R$ to complete the loop?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: At the topmost point, tension $T \ge 0 \implies v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gR}$. By energy conservation, $v_{\text{bottom}} = \sqrt{v_{\text{top}}^2 + 4gR} = \sqrt{5gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum speed $v_{\text{top}}$ at the topmost point of a vertical circle of radius $R$ for tension not to become negative?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force
questions.explanation: At the peak, gravity provides centripetal acceleration when string goes slack ($T = 0$): $\frac{mv^2}{R} = mg \implies v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the coefficient of restitution $e$ defined in terms of separation and approach velocities?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Work Done by Constant & Variable Force

questions.prompt: What is the loss of kinetic energy $\Delta K$ during a completely inelastic collision between masses $m_1$ and $m_2$?

questions.prompt: What is the elastic potential energy $U_s$ stored in a spring with spring constant $k$ stretched by elongation $x$?

sets.title: Set 1: Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems

questions.prompt: What is the relation between torque $\vec{\tau}$, moment of inertia $I$, and angular acceleration $\vec{\alpha}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Rotational analogue of $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$ is $\vec{\tau} = I\vec{\alpha} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What is the statement of the Parallel Axis Theorem for moment of inertia?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia about any parallel axis at distance $d$ from the center of mass axis is $I = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its diameter?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: For a solid sphere, integrating spherical shells yields $I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2$. (For hollow sphere it is $\frac{2}{3}MR^2$).

questions.prompt: What is the total kinetic energy $K_{\text{total}}$ of a body of mass $M$ rolling purely without slipping?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems

questions.prompt: What is the acceleration $a$ of a body with radius of gyration $k$ rolling down an incline of angle $\theta$ without slipping?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Applying torque balance and linear force equation yields $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + k^2/R^2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the angular momentum $\vec{L}$ of a rigid body rotating with angular velocity $\vec{\omega}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is defined as moment of momentum $\vec{r}\times\vec{p} = I\vec{\omega}$.

questions.prompt: What is the statement of the Perpendicular Axis Theorem for a flat 2D lamina in the $xy$-plane?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: For a 2D planar object, moment of inertia about the normal z-axis equals sum of moments about orthogonal in-plane axes: $I_z = I_x + I_y$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its central perpendicular axis?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Integrating concentric rings of radius $r$ gives $I = \int_0^R (2\pi r\,dr \sigma) r^2 = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of length $L$ and mass $M$ about an axis through its center perpendicular to its length?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Integrating from $-L/2$ to $+L/2$: $I = \int_{-L/2}^{L/2} \lambda x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{12}ML^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a thin rod of length $L$ about an axis passing through one of its ends?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Center of Mass of Discrete & Continuous Systems
questions.explanation: Using parallel axis theorem: $I = I_{\text{cm}} + M(L/2)^2 = \frac{1}{12}ML^2 + \frac{1}{4}ML^2 = \frac{1}{3}ML^2$.

questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: For a 2D planar object, moment of inertia about the normal z-axis equals sum of moments about orthogonal in-plane axes: $I_z = I_x + I_y$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its central perpendicular axis?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Integrating concentric rings of radius $r$ gives $I = \int_0^R (2\pi r\,dr \sigma) r^2 = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of length $L$ and mass $M$ about an axis through its center perpendicular to its length?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Integrating from $-L/2$ to $+L/2$: $I = \int_{-L/2}^{L/2} \lambda x^2\,dx = \frac{1}{12}ML^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a thin rod of length $L$ about an axis passing through one of its ends?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Using parallel axis theorem: $I = I_{\text{cm}} + M(L/2)^2 = \frac{1}{12}ML^2 + \frac{1}{4}ML^2 = \frac{1}{3}ML^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between torque $\vec{\tau}$, moment of inertia $I$, and angular acceleration $\vec{\alpha}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Rotational analogue of $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$ is $\vec{\tau} = I\vec{\alpha} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What is the statement of the Parallel Axis Theorem for moment of inertia?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia about any parallel axis at distance $d$ from the center of mass axis is $I = I_{\text{cm}} + Md^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about its diameter?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: For a solid sphere, integrating spherical shells yields $I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2$. (For hollow sphere it is $\frac{2}{3}MR^2$).

questions.prompt: What is the total kinetic energy $K_{\text{total}}$ of a body of mass $M$ rolling purely without slipping?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law

questions.prompt: What is the acceleration $a$ of a body with radius of gyration $k$ rolling down an incline of angle $\theta$ without slipping?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Applying torque balance and linear force equation yields $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + k^2/R^2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the angular momentum $\vec{L}$ of a rigid body rotating with angular velocity $\vec{\omega}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Angular Momentum & Conservation Law
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is defined as moment of momentum $\vec{r}\times\vec{p} = I\vec{\omega}$.

sets.title: Set 1: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation

questions.prompt: What is Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation in vector form?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is attractive along the line joining the centers: $\vec{F}_{12} = -\frac{Gm_1 m_2}{r^2}\hat{r}_{12}$.

questions.prompt: What is the escape velocity $v_e$ from the surface of Earth (radius $R$, mass $M$)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Setting total mechanical energy $\frac{1}{2}mv_e^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0 \implies v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{2gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the orbital velocity $v_o$ of a satellite revolving close to Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Equating gravitational pull to centripetal force: $\frac{mv_o^2}{R} = \frac{GMm}{R^2} \implies v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R}} = \sqrt{gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the exact ratio of escape velocity to orbital velocity ($v_e / v_o$)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: $$v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$$ and $$v_o = \sqrt{gR}$$. Therefore, $$v_e / v_o = \sqrt{2}$$.

questions.prompt: How does acceleration due to gravity vary at altitude $h \ll R$ above Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: $$g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2} = g\left(1 + \frac{h}{R}\right)^{-2} \approx g\left(1 - \frac{2h}{R}\right)$$ using binomial theorem.

questions.prompt: How does acceleration due to gravity vary at depth $d$ below Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Inside Earth at distance $r = R - d$, mass enclosed is $M' = M\frac{r^3}{R^3}$. Hence $g_d = g\frac{r}{R} = g(1 - d/R)$.

questions.prompt: What is Kepler's Third Law (Harmonic Law) relating satellite time period $T$ and orbital radius $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Equating orbital speed $v = \frac{2\pi r}{T}$ and $v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$ gives $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{GM}r^3$.

questions.prompt: What is the gravitational potential energy $U(r)$ of a two-body system ($M, m$) separated by distance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Taking reference potential energy $U(\infty) = 0$, work done bringing mass from infinity is negative: $U = -\frac{GMm}{r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the total mechanical energy $E$ of an orbiting satellite of mass $m$ at distance $r$ from Earth's center?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is $K = \frac{GMm}{2r}$ and potential energy is $U = -\frac{GMm}{r}$. Total energy is $E = K + U = -\frac{GMm}{2r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the time period of a geostationary satellite revolving above Earth's equator?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite has orbital period equal to Earth's rotational period ($T = 24\text{ hours}$) and orbits from west to east.

sets.title: Set 8: Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites

questions.prompt: What is the escape velocity $v_e$ from the surface of Earth (radius $R$, mass $M$)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Setting total mechanical energy $\frac{1}{2}mv_e^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0 \implies v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{2gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the orbital velocity $v_o$ of a satellite revolving close to Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Equating gravitational pull to centripetal force: $\frac{mv_o^2}{R} = \frac{GMm}{R^2} \implies v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R}} = \sqrt{gR}$.

questions.prompt: What is the exact ratio of escape velocity to orbital velocity ($v_e / v_o$)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: $$v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$$ and $$v_o = \sqrt{gR}$$. Therefore, $$v_e / v_o = \sqrt{2}$$.

questions.prompt: How does acceleration due to gravity vary at altitude $h \ll R$ above Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: $$g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2} = g\left(1 + \frac{h}{R}\right)^{-2} \approx g\left(1 - \frac{2h}{R}\right)$$ using binomial theorem.

questions.prompt: How does acceleration due to gravity vary at depth $d$ below Earth's surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Inside Earth at distance $r = R - d$, mass enclosed is $M' = M\frac{r^3}{R^3}$. Hence $g_d = g\frac{r}{R} = g(1 - d/R)$.

questions.prompt: What is Kepler's Third Law (Harmonic Law) relating satellite time period $T$ and orbital radius $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Equating orbital speed $v = \frac{2\pi r}{T}$ and $v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$ gives $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{GM}r^3$.

questions.prompt: What is the gravitational potential energy $U(r)$ of a two-body system ($M, m$) separated by distance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Taking reference potential energy $U(\infty) = 0$, work done bringing mass from infinity is negative: $U = -\frac{GMm}{r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the total mechanical energy $E$ of an orbiting satellite of mass $m$ at distance $r$ from Earth's center?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is $K = \frac{GMm}{2r}$ and potential energy is $U = -\frac{GMm}{r}$. Total energy is $E = K + U = -\frac{GMm}{2r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the time period of a geostationary satellite revolving above Earth's equator?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite has orbital period equal to Earth's rotational period ($T = 24\text{ hours}$) and orbits from west to east.

questions.prompt: What is Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation in vector form?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Orbital Velocity of Artificial Satellites
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is attractive along the line joining the centers: $\vec{F}_{12} = -\frac{Gm_1 m_2}{r^2}\hat{r}_{12}$.

sets.title: Set 1: First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)

questions.prompt: What is the microscopic relation connecting electric current $I$ and electron drift velocity $v_d$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Total charge flowing per second is $q/t = (n A v_d t e)/t = n e A v_d$, where $n$ is free electron density.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for drift velocity $v_d$ in terms of electric field $E$ and relaxation time $\tau$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Acceleration of electron under electric field is $a = \frac{eE}{m}$. Average drift acquired during relaxation time is $v_d = a\tau = \frac{eE\tau}{m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between current density $\vec{J}$, conductivity $\sigma$, and electric field $\vec{E}$ (Microscopic Ohm's Law)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: $$J = \frac{I}{A} = n e v_d = n e \left(\frac{e E \tau}{m}\right) = \left(\frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}\right) E = \sigma E$$.

questions.prompt: What is the electrical resistance $R$ of a uniform conductor of length $l$, cross-sectional area $A$, and resistivity $\rho$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to area: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$.

questions.prompt: What is the temperature dependence formula for resistance $R_T$ at temperature $T$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Fractional change in resistance is proportional to temperature rise: $\frac{\Delta R}{R_0} = \alpha \Delta T \implies R_T = R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between cell EMF $\mathcal{E}$, internal resistance $r$, current $I$, and terminal potential $V$ during discharge?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: During discharging, internal voltage drop $Ir$ reduces output terminal potential: $V = \mathcal{E} - Ir$.

questions.prompt: What is the balance condition for a Wheatstone Bridge circuit with four arms $P, Q, R, S$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: When galvanometer current is zero ($I_g = 0$), the potential across diagonal points is equal, giving $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for unknown resistance $S$ using a Metre Bridge with balancing length $l\text{ cm}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Since wire resistance is proportional to length: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies S = R\frac{100 - l}{l}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem condition for an external load $R$ connected to a cell with internal resistance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: Differentiating $P = I^2 R = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 R}{(R+r)^2}$ with respect to $R$ and equating to zero yields $R = r$, giving $P_{\max} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2}{4r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent EMF $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}}$ and internal resistance $r_{\text{eq}}$ for two cells $\mathcal{E}_1, r_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2, r_2$ in parallel?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW)
questions.explanation: By Millman's Theorem / Kirchhoff's rules, $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\mathcal{E}_1/r_1 + \mathcal{E}_2/r_2}{1/r_1 + 1/r_2}$ and $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between cell EMF $\mathcal{E}$, internal resistance $r$, current $I$, and terminal potential $V$ during discharge?

questions.prompt: What is the balance condition for a Wheatstone Bridge circuit with four arms $P, Q, R, S$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula
questions.explanation: When galvanometer current is zero ($I_g = 0$), the potential across diagonal points is equal, giving $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for unknown resistance $S$ using a Metre Bridge with balancing length $l\text{ cm}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula
questions.explanation: Since wire resistance is proportional to length: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies S = R\frac{100 - l}{l}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem condition for an external load $R$ connected to a cell with internal resistance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula
questions.explanation: Differentiating $P = I^2 R = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 R}{(R+r)^2}$ with respect to $R$ and equating to zero yields $R = r$, giving $P_{\max} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2}{4r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent EMF $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}}$ and internal resistance $r_{\text{eq}}$ for two cells $\mathcal{E}_1, r_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2, r_2$ in parallel?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula
questions.explanation: By Millman's Theorem / Kirchhoff's rules, $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\mathcal{E}_1/r_1 + \mathcal{E}_2/r_2}{1/r_1 + 1/r_2}$ and $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the microscopic relation connecting electric current $I$ and electron drift velocity $v_d$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula

questions.prompt: What is the formula for drift velocity $v_d$ in terms of electric field $E$ and relaxation time $\tau$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Carnot Engine Efficiency Formula
questions.explanation: Acceleration of electron under electric field is $a = \frac{eE}{m}$. Average drift acquired during relaxation time is $v_d = a\tau = \frac{eE\tau}{m}$.

sets.title: Set 1: Simple Harmonic Motion Differential Equation
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Simple Harmonic Motion Differential Equation

questions.prompt: What is the Biot-Savart Law expressing magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ due to a current element $I\,d\vec{l}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Simple Harmonic Motion Differential Equation
questions.explanation: Biot-Savart law in vector form is $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\hat{r})}{r^2} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\vec{r})}{r^3}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic field $B$ at the center of a circular loop of radius $R$ carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Simple Harmonic Motion Differential Equation
questions.explanation: Integrating around circle: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2}(2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

questions.explanation: Integrating around circle: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2}(2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic field $B$ inside an infinitely long ideal solenoid with $n$ turns per unit length carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: By Ampere's circuital law: $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = B L = \mu_0(n L)I \implies B = \mu_0 n I$.

questions.prompt: What is the Lorentz Force equation on a charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in electric and magnetic fields?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: The net electromagnetic force consists of electric force $q\vec{E}$ and magnetic force $q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v}\times\vec{B})$.

questions.prompt: What is the radius $r$ of the helical or circular path of a charged particle ($q, m$) in a perpendicular magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Magnetic Lorentz force provides centripetal acceleration: $q v B = \frac{m v^2}{r} \implies r = \frac{mv}{qB}$.

questions.prompt: What is the cyclotron frequency $\nu$ of a charged particle in magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Time period $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$. Frequency is reciprocal: $\nu = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic force per unit length $\frac{F}{L}$ between two long parallel wires separated by distance $d$ carrying currents $I_1, I_2$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Field produced by wire 1 is $B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$. Force on wire 2 is $F = I_2 L B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$.

questions.prompt: What is Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction for induced EMF $\mathcal{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Magnitude of induced EMF is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux, and the negative sign represents Lenz's Law: $\mathcal{E} = -\frac{d\Phi_B}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What is the motional EMF $\mathcal{E}$ induced in a straight conductor of length $l$ moving with velocity $v$ perpendicular to field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Lorentz force on free electrons is $q v B$. The induced potential difference across the ends of length $l$ is $\mathcal{E} = E l = (vB)l = Blv$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic energy $U_B$ stored in an inductor of self-inductance $L$ carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Work done against self-induced back EMF: $U = \int_0^I L i\,di = \frac{1}{2}LI^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the Biot-Savart Law expressing magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ due to a current element $I\,d\vec{l}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Standing Waves in Stretched Strings & Harmonics
questions.explanation: Biot-Savart law in vector form is $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\hat{r})}{r^2} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\vec{r})}{r^3}$.

sets.title: Set 1: Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form

questions.prompt: What is Coulomb's Law expressing the electrostatic force between two point charges in vacuum?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: In SI units, $\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \approx 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$, and force is $F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$.

questions.prompt: What is Gauss's Law in electrostatics relating total electric flux $\Phi_E$ through a closed Gaussian surface?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Gauss's Law states that total outward electric flux through any closed surface is proportional to net enclosed charge: $\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.prompt: What is the capacitance $C$ of a parallel-plate capacitor with plate area $A$ and separation $d$ in vacuum?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Electric field between plates is $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}$. Voltage $V = Ed = \frac{Qd}{\varepsilon_0 A}$. Therefore $C = \frac{Q}{V} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$.

questions.prompt: What is the capacitance when a dielectric slab of dielectric constant $K$ completely fills the space between plates?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: A dielectric reduces the electric field by factor $K$, reducing voltage to $V/K$, thus increasing capacitance by factor $K$: $C' = KC_0$.

questions.prompt: What is the total electrostatic energy $U$ stored in a charged capacitor of capacitance $C$ at potential $V$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Work done charging capacitor is $U = \int_0^Q \frac{q}{C}\,dq = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac{1}{2}CV^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the electrostatic energy density $u_E$ (energy per unit volume) in an electric field $E$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Dividing total energy $U = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0(A/d)(Ed)^2$ by volume $Ad$ yields $u_E = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent capacitance $C_{\text{eq}}$ for two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ connected in series?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: In series, charge $Q$ is identical on both plates while voltages add: $V = V_1 + V_2 \implies \frac{Q}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{Q}{C_1} + \frac{Q}{C_2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the torque $\vec{\tau}$ experienced by an electric dipole $\vec{p}$ in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Forces on $+q$ and $-q$ form a couple: torque $\tau = qE(2a\sin\theta) = pE\sin\theta$, or $\vec{\tau} = \vec{p}\times\vec{E}$.

questions.prompt: What is the potential energy $U$ of an electric dipole $\vec{p}$ aligned at angle $\theta$ in electric field $\vec{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: Work done rotating dipole from $90^\circ$ to $\theta$ is $U = \int_{90^\circ}^\theta pE\sin\theta\,d\theta = -pE\cos\theta = -\vec{p}\cdot\vec{E}$.

questions.prompt: What is the electric field $E$ on the axial line of a short electric dipole ($r \gg 2a$)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Coulomb's Law in Vector & Scalar Form
questions.explanation: For a short dipole, the electric field on the axial axis is double the equatorial field: $E_{\text{axial}} = \frac{2kp}{r^3}$.

questions.explanation: Work done charging capacitor is $U = \int_0^Q \frac{q}{C}\,dq = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac{1}{2}CV^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the electrostatic energy density $u_E$ (energy per unit volume) in an electric field $E$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Gauss's Law & Electric Flux
questions.explanation: Dividing total energy $U = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0(A/d)(Ed)^2$ by volume $Ad$ yields $u_E = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent capacitance $C_{\text{eq}}$ for two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ connected in series?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Gauss's Law & Electric Flux
questions.explanation: In series, charge $Q$ is identical on both plates while voltages add: $V = V_1 + V_2 \implies \frac{Q}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{Q}{C_1} + \frac{Q}{C_2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the torque $\vec{\tau}$ experienced by an electric dipole $\vec{p}$ in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Gauss's Law & Electric Flux
questions.explanation: Forces on $+q$ and $-q$ form a couple: torque $\tau = qE(2a\sin\theta) = pE\sin\theta$, or $\vec{\tau} = \vec{p}\times\vec{E}$.

questions.prompt: What is the potential energy $U$ of an electric dipole $\vec{p}$ aligned at angle $\theta$ in electric field $\vec{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Gauss's Law & Electric Flux
questions.explanation: Work done rotating dipole from $90^\circ$ to $\theta$ is $U = \int_{90^\circ}^\theta pE\sin\theta\,d\theta = -pE\cos\theta = -\vec{p}\cdot\vec{E}$.

sets.title: Set 5: Electric Potential Due to Point Charge & Dipole
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Electric Potential Due to Point Charge & Dipole

questions.prompt: What is the capacitance $C$ of a parallel-plate capacitor with plate area $A$ and separation $d$ in vacuum?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Electric Potential Due to Point Charge & Dipole
questions.explanation: Electric field between plates is $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0 A}$. Voltage $V = Ed = \frac{Qd}{\varepsilon_0 A}$. Therefore $C = \frac{Q}{V} = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$.

questions.prompt: What is the capacitance when a dielectric slab of dielectric constant $K$ completely fills the space between plates?

sets.title: Set 1: Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time

questions.prompt: What is the microscopic relation connecting electric current $I$ and electron drift velocity $v_d$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Total charge flowing per second is $q/t = (n A v_d t e)/t = n e A v_d$, where $n$ is free electron density.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for drift velocity $v_d$ in terms of electric field $E$ and relaxation time $\tau$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Acceleration of electron under electric field is $a = \frac{eE}{m}$. Average drift acquired during relaxation time is $v_d = a\tau = \frac{eE\tau}{m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between current density $\vec{J}$, conductivity $\sigma$, and electric field $\vec{E}$ (Microscopic Ohm's Law)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: $$J = \frac{I}{A} = n e v_d = n e \left(\frac{e E \tau}{m}\right) = \left(\frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}\right) E = \sigma E$$.

questions.prompt: What is the electrical resistance $R$ of a uniform conductor of length $l$, cross-sectional area $A$, and resistivity $\rho$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to area: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$.

questions.prompt: What is the temperature dependence formula for resistance $R_T$ at temperature $T$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Fractional change in resistance is proportional to temperature rise: $\frac{\Delta R}{R_0} = \alpha \Delta T \implies R_T = R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between cell EMF $\mathcal{E}$, internal resistance $r$, current $I$, and terminal potential $V$ during discharge?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: During discharging, internal voltage drop $Ir$ reduces output terminal potential: $V = \mathcal{E} - Ir$.

questions.prompt: What is the balance condition for a Wheatstone Bridge circuit with four arms $P, Q, R, S$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: When galvanometer current is zero ($I_g = 0$), the potential across diagonal points is equal, giving $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for unknown resistance $S$ using a Metre Bridge with balancing length $l\text{ cm}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Since wire resistance is proportional to length: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies S = R\frac{100 - l}{l}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem condition for an external load $R$ connected to a cell with internal resistance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: Differentiating $P = I^2 R = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 R}{(R+r)^2}$ with respect to $R$ and equating to zero yields $R = r$, giving $P_{\max} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2}{4r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent EMF $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}}$ and internal resistance $r_{\text{eq}}$ for two cells $\mathcal{E}_1, r_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2, r_2$ in parallel?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity & Relaxation Time
questions.explanation: By Millman's Theorem / Kirchhoff's rules, $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\mathcal{E}_1/r_1 + \mathcal{E}_2/r_2}{1/r_1 + 1/r_2}$ and $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$.

questions.explanation: Since wire resistance is proportional to length: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies S = R\frac{100 - l}{l}$.

sets.title: Set 8: Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition

questions.prompt: What is the formula for drift velocity $v_d$ in terms of electric field $E$ and relaxation time $\tau$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Acceleration of electron under electric field is $a = \frac{eE}{m}$. Average drift acquired during relaxation time is $v_d = a\tau = \frac{eE\tau}{m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between current density $\vec{J}$, conductivity $\sigma$, and electric field $\vec{E}$ (Microscopic Ohm's Law)?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: $$J = \frac{I}{A} = n e v_d = n e \left(\frac{e E \tau}{m}\right) = \left(\frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}\right) E = \sigma E$$.

questions.prompt: What is the electrical resistance $R$ of a uniform conductor of length $l$, cross-sectional area $A$, and resistivity $\rho$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to area: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$.

questions.prompt: What is the temperature dependence formula for resistance $R_T$ at temperature $T$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Fractional change in resistance is proportional to temperature rise: $\frac{\Delta R}{R_0} = \alpha \Delta T \implies R_T = R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between cell EMF $\mathcal{E}$, internal resistance $r$, current $I$, and terminal potential $V$ during discharge?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: During discharging, internal voltage drop $Ir$ reduces output terminal potential: $V = \mathcal{E} - Ir$.

questions.prompt: What is the balance condition for a Wheatstone Bridge circuit with four arms $P, Q, R, S$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: When galvanometer current is zero ($I_g = 0$), the potential across diagonal points is equal, giving $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for unknown resistance $S$ using a Metre Bridge with balancing length $l\text{ cm}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Since wire resistance is proportional to length: $\frac{R}{S} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \implies S = R\frac{100 - l}{l}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem condition for an external load $R$ connected to a cell with internal resistance $r$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Differentiating $P = I^2 R = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 R}{(R+r)^2}$ with respect to $R$ and equating to zero yields $R = r$, giving $P_{\max} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2}{4r}$.

questions.prompt: What is the equivalent EMF $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}}$ and internal resistance $r_{\text{eq}}$ for two cells $\mathcal{E}_1, r_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2, r_2$ in parallel?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: By Millman's Theorem / Kirchhoff's rules, $\mathcal{E}_{\text{eq}} = \frac{\mathcal{E}_1/r_1 + \mathcal{E}_2/r_2}{1/r_1 + 1/r_2}$ and $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the microscopic relation connecting electric current $I$ and electron drift velocity $v_d$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition
questions.explanation: Total charge flowing per second is $q/t = (n A v_d t e)/t = n e A v_d$, where $n$ is free electron density.

sets.title: Set 1: Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field

questions.prompt: What is the Biot-Savart Law expressing magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ due to a current element $I\,d\vec{l}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Biot-Savart law in vector form is $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\hat{r})}{r^2} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I(d\vec{l}\times\vec{r})}{r^3}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic field $B$ at the center of a circular loop of radius $R$ carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Integrating around circle: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R^2}(2\pi R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic field $B$ inside an infinitely long ideal solenoid with $n$ turns per unit length carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: By Ampere's circuital law: $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = B L = \mu_0(n L)I \implies B = \mu_0 n I$.

questions.prompt: What is the Lorentz Force equation on a charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in electric and magnetic fields?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: The net electromagnetic force consists of electric force $q\vec{E}$ and magnetic force $q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v}\times\vec{B})$.

questions.prompt: What is the radius $r$ of the helical or circular path of a charged particle ($q, m$) in a perpendicular magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Magnetic Lorentz force provides centripetal acceleration: $q v B = \frac{m v^2}{r} \implies r = \frac{mv}{qB}$.

questions.prompt: What is the cyclotron frequency $\nu$ of a charged particle in magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Time period $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$. Frequency is reciprocal: $\nu = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic force per unit length $\frac{F}{L}$ between two long parallel wires separated by distance $d$ carrying currents $I_1, I_2$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Field produced by wire 1 is $B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$. Force on wire 2 is $F = I_2 L B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$.

questions.prompt: What is Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction for induced EMF $\mathcal{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Magnitude of induced EMF is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux, and the negative sign represents Lenz's Law: $\mathcal{E} = -\frac{d\Phi_B}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What is the motional EMF $\mathcal{E}$ induced in a straight conductor of length $l$ moving with velocity $v$ perpendicular to field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Lorentz force on free electrons is $q v B$. The induced potential difference across the ends of length $l$ is $\mathcal{E} = E l = (vB)l = Blv$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic energy $U_B$ stored in an inductor of self-inductance $L$ carrying current $I$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Biot-Savart Law for Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: Work done against self-induced back EMF: $U = \int_0^I L i\,di = \frac{1}{2}LI^2$.

questions.explanation: The net electromagnetic force consists of electric force $q\vec{E}$ and magnetic force $q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v}\times\vec{B})$.

questions.prompt: What is the radius $r$ of the helical or circular path of a charged particle ($q, m$) in a perpendicular magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Lorentz Force & Motion in Magnetic Field (Cyclotron)
questions.explanation: Magnetic Lorentz force provides centripetal acceleration: $q v B = \frac{m v^2}{r} \implies r = \frac{mv}{qB}$.

questions.prompt: What is the cyclotron frequency $\nu$ of a charged particle in magnetic field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Lorentz Force & Motion in Magnetic Field (Cyclotron)
questions.explanation: Time period $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$. Frequency is reciprocal: $\nu = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$.

questions.prompt: What is the magnetic force per unit length $\frac{F}{L}$ between two long parallel wires separated by distance $d$ carrying currents $I_1, I_2$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Lorentz Force & Motion in Magnetic Field (Cyclotron)
questions.explanation: Field produced by wire 1 is $B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$. Force on wire 2 is $F = I_2 L B = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$.

questions.prompt: What is Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction for induced EMF $\mathcal{E}$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Lorentz Force & Motion in Magnetic Field (Cyclotron)
questions.explanation: Magnitude of induced EMF is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux, and the negative sign represents Lenz's Law: $\mathcal{E} = -\frac{d\Phi_B}{dt}$.

questions.prompt: What is the motional EMF $\mathcal{E}$ induced in a straight conductor of length $l$ moving with velocity $v$ perpendicular to field $B$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Lorentz Force & Motion in Magnetic Field (Cyclotron)
questions.explanation: Lorentz force on free electrons is $q v B$. The induced potential difference across the ends of length $l$ is $\mathcal{E} = E l = (vB)l = Blv$.

sets.title: Set 1: RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage

questions.prompt: What is the impedance $Z$ of a series $LCR$ alternating current circuit?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Using phasor addition of voltages $V_R, V_L, V_C$: $V^2 = V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2 \implies Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

questions.prompt: What is the resonant frequency $\omega_0$ and $f_0$ of a series $LCR$ circuit?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when inductive and capacitive reactances cancel: $X_L = X_C \implies \omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C} \implies \omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the power factor $\cos\phi$ of a series $LCR$ alternating current circuit?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: From the impedance triangle, base is $R$ and hypotenuse is $Z$: power factor $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between root-mean-square value $I_{\text{rms}}$ and peak value $I_0$ of sinusoidal AC?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Integrating $I^2 = I_0^2\sin^2(\omega t)$ over one full cycle yields $I_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_0^2}{2}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Thin Lens Formula relating focal length $f$, object distance $u$, and image distance $v$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: By Cartesian sign convention, the thin lens equation is $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u}$ (unlike mirror equation which is $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}$).

questions.prompt: What is the Lens Maker's Formula for a lens of refractive index $\mu$ with surface radii $R_1$ and $R_2$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Refraction through two curved spherical surfaces leads to the Lens Maker's Formula: $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$.

questions.prompt: What is the Mirror Formula relating object distance $u$, image distance $v$, and focal length $f$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: For all spherical mirrors (concave and convex) under Cartesian sign conventions: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between refractive index $\mu$ of a prism, angle of prism $A$, and angle of minimum deviation $D_m$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation, angle of incidence equals angle of emergence ($i_1 = i_2 = \frac{A+D_m}{2}$) and internal angles $r_1 = r_2 = \frac{A}{2}$, yielding $\mu = \frac{\sin((A+D_m)/2)}{\sin(A/2)}$.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for critical angle $\theta_c$ for Total Internal Reflection at a medium boundary of refractive index $\mu$ into air?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Applying Snell's law $\mu\sin\theta_c = 1\cdot\sin(90^\circ) = 1 \implies \sin\theta_c = \frac{1}{\mu}$.

questions.prompt: What is the total optical power $P$ of two thin lenses of powers $P_1$ and $P_2$ kept in contact?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • RMS & Peak Values of Alternating Current and Voltage
questions.explanation: Optical powers are additive when lenses are in contact: $P = P_1 + P_2$.

questions.explanation: Refraction through two curved spherical surfaces leads to the Lens Maker's Formula: $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$.

questions.prompt: What is the Mirror Formula relating object distance $u$, image distance $v$, and focal length $f$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Spherical Mirrors Formula & Magnification
questions.explanation: For all spherical mirrors (concave and convex) under Cartesian sign conventions: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between refractive index $\mu$ of a prism, angle of prism $A$, and angle of minimum deviation $D_m$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Spherical Mirrors Formula & Magnification
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation, angle of incidence equals angle of emergence ($i_1 = i_2 = \frac{A+D_m}{2}$) and internal angles $r_1 = r_2 = \frac{A}{2}$, yielding $\mu = \frac{\sin((A+D_m)/2)}{\sin(A/2)}$.

sets.title: Set 8: Snell's Law & Critical Angle (Total Internal Reflection)

questions.prompt: What is the resonant frequency $\omega_0$ and $f_0$ of a series $LCR$ circuit?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Snell's Law & Critical Angle (Total Internal Reflection)
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when inductive and capacitive reactances cancel: $X_L = X_C \implies \omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C} \implies \omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the power factor $\cos\phi$ of a series $LCR$ alternating current circuit?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Snell's Law & Critical Angle (Total Internal Reflection)
questions.explanation: From the impedance triangle, base is $R$ and hypotenuse is $Z$: power factor $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}$.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between root-mean-square value $I_{\text{rms}}$ and peak value $I_0$ of sinusoidal AC?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Snell's Law & Critical Angle (Total Internal Reflection)
questions.explanation: Integrating $I^2 = I_0^2\sin^2(\omega t)$ over one full cycle yields $I_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_0^2}{2}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.explanation: Applying Snell's law $\mu\sin\theta_c = 1\cdot\sin(90^\circ) = 1 \implies \sin\theta_c = \frac{1}{\mu}$.

sets.title: Set 1: Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
sets.description: 10 CBSE MCQ Formula questions on Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)

questions.prompt: What is the fringe width $\beta$ in Young's Double Slit Experiment (YDSE) with slit separation $d$, screen distance $D$, and wavelength $\lambda$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: Fringe width is the separation between consecutive bright or dark fringes: $\beta = y_{n+1} - y_n = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.

questions.prompt: What is Einstein's Photoelectric Equation for maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ of emitted photoelectrons?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation:
Photon energy $h
u$ supplies work function $\phi_0$ and kinetic energy: $h
u = \phi_0 + K_{\max} \implies K_{\max} = h
u - \phi_0 = eV_0$ (where $V_0$ is stopping potential).

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of a matter wave with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $E$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: De Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$. Expressing momentum via kinetic energy $p = \sqrt{2mE}$ gives $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential difference $V$ volts?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: Substituting constants ($h, m_e, e$) into $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e e V}}$ yields $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{\AA}$.

questions.prompt: What is the energy $E_n$ of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of Hydrogen atom?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: Electrostatic attraction and Bohr's angular momentum postulate $L = n\frac{h}{2\pi}$ yield total energy $E_n = -\frac{me^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2} = -\frac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Rydberg Formula for wavenumber $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$ of spectral lines in Hydrogen?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: $$\Delta E = E_{n_2} - E_{n_1} = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \implies \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$$, where $R_H \approx 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}$.

questions.prompt: What is the half-life $T_{1/2}$ of a radioactive isotope with decay constant $\lambda$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: By decay law $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. At $N = N_0/2$, $e^{\lambda T_{1/2}} = 2 \implies T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$.

questions.prompt: What is the mass defect $\Delta m$ and binding energy $E_b$ of a nucleus with $Z$ protons and $N = A - Z$ neutrons?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: Einstein's mass-energy relation states $E_b = \Delta m\,c^2$, where $\Delta m$ is the difference between constituent nucleon masses and bound nucleus mass.

questions.prompt: What is the mass-action law relating electron density $n_e$, hole density $n_h$, and intrinsic carrier density $n_i$ in a semiconductor?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: Under thermal equilibrium, the product of electron and hole concentration is constant and equal to $n_i^2$.

questions.prompt: What is Brewster's Law relating polarizing angle $i_p$ to refractive index $\mu$ of the medium?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Young's Double Slit Experiment Fringe Width (β)
questions.explanation: When the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular ($i_p + r = 90^\circ$), reflected light is completely plane-polarized: $\mu = \frac{\sin i_p}{\cos i_p} = \tan i_p$.

questions.explanation: When the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular ($i_p + r = 90^\circ$), reflected light is completely plane-polarized: $\mu = \frac{\sin i_p}{\cos i_p} = \tan i_p$.

questions.prompt: What is the fringe width $\beta$ in Young's Double Slit Experiment (YDSE) with slit separation $d$, screen distance $D$, and wavelength $\lambda$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Cut-off Voltage
questions.explanation: Fringe width is the separation between consecutive bright or dark fringes: $\beta = y_{n+1} - y_n = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.

questions.prompt: What is Einstein's Photoelectric Equation for maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ of emitted photoelectrons?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Cut-off Voltage
questions.explanation:
Photon energy $h
u$ supplies work function $\phi_0$ and kinetic energy: $h
u = \phi_0 + K_{\max} \implies K_{\max} = h
u - \phi_0 = eV_0$ (where $V_0$ is stopping potential).

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of a matter wave with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $E$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Cut-off Voltage
questions.explanation: De Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$. Expressing momentum via kinetic energy $p = \sqrt{2mE}$ gives $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential difference $V$ volts?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Cut-off Voltage
questions.explanation: Substituting constants ($h, m_e, e$) into $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e e V}}$ yields $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{\AA}$.

questions.prompt: What is the energy $E_n$ of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of Hydrogen atom?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Cut-off Voltage
questions.explanation: Electrostatic attraction and Bohr's angular momentum postulate $L = n\frac{h}{2\pi}$ yield total energy $E_n = -\frac{me^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2} = -\frac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Rydberg Formula for wavenumber $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$ of spectral lines in Hydrogen?

questions.prompt: What is the half-life $T_{1/2}$ of a radioactive isotope with decay constant $\lambda$?

questions.prompt: What is the mass-action law relating electron density $n_e$, hole density $n_h$, and intrinsic carrier density $n_i$ in a semiconductor?

questions.explanation: Under thermal equilibrium, the product of electron and hole concentration is constant and equal to $n_i^2$.

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of a matter wave with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $E$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Semiconductor Carrier Density & p-n Junction Rectifier
questions.explanation: De Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$. Expressing momentum via kinetic energy $p = \sqrt{2mE}$ gives $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$.

questions.prompt: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential difference $V$ volts?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Semiconductor Carrier Density & p-n Junction Rectifier
questions.explanation: Substituting constants ($h, m_e, e$) into $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m_e e V}}$ yields $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{\AA}$.

questions.prompt: What is the energy $E_n$ of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of Hydrogen atom?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Semiconductor Carrier Density & p-n Junction Rectifier
questions.explanation: Electrostatic attraction and Bohr's angular momentum postulate $L = n\frac{h}{2\pi}$ yield total energy $E_n = -\frac{me^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2} = -\frac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}$.

questions.prompt: What is the Rydberg Formula for wavenumber $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$ of spectral lines in Hydrogen?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Semiconductor Carrier Density & p-n Junction Rectifier
questions.explanation: $$\Delta E = E_{n_2} - E_{n_1} = \frac{hc}{\lambda} \implies \frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$$, where $R_H \approx 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}$.

questions.prompt: What is the half-life $T_{1/2}$ of a radioactive isotope with decay constant $\lambda$?
questions.subPrompt: CBSE Chapter Formula Test • Semiconductor Carrier Density & p-n Junction Rectifier
questions.explanation: By decay law $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. At $N = N_0/2$, $e^{\lambda T_{1/2}} = 2 \implies T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$.
